title: Autos & Vehicles Ecommerce Benchmarks for 2026
summary: Conversion rate, average order value, and bounce rate reporting for the Autos & Vehicles ecommerce category in 2026.
body_markdown:
## Still the Highest AOV in the Dataset — But Conversion Fell Sharply in Q3


The benchmarks:[1.26% median CVR](https://getshogun.com/benchmarks/ecommerce-conversion-rate) ,[$601 median AOV](https://getshogun.com/benchmarks/ecommerce-average-order-value) . Autos & Vehicles has the highest median order value of any category in the dataset — and one of the lowest conversion rates. That combination is not a contradiction. It is how considered-purchase categories tend to behave.


Source: Shogun 2026 Year-to-Date Ecommerce Benchmark Reports (January–September 2026), Autos & Vehicles.


Q3 was a hard quarter for conversion. Among the 25 stores active in both Q2 and Q3, CVR fell 33.6% — the steepest decline of any published category — compared with a 7.7% rise over the same quarters in 2025. The matched group is small, so treat the exact figure as directional, but the monthly data shows the same thing: July (1.06%), August (0.87%) and September (0.84%) were the three lowest months in the 21-month window. Order value held up better. Same-store AOV slipped 3.5% from Q2 to Q3 ($625 to $603 across 92 stores) but is up 17.9% year over year — the largest gain of any reported category.


The P25-to-P75 AOV range is $319–$1,026 — a 3.2× spread. That span reflects a category where some merchants are selling parts and accessories and others are selling high-ticket equipment or vehicles directly. The median ($601) sits well above the cross-industry median of $313.


> ***Autos & Vehicles has the highest median AOV in the 2026 year-to-date dataset at $601 — nearly double the cross-industry median of $313 — and the largest year-over-year AOV gain (+17.9%) of any reported category. The trade-off: the category’s 1.26% CVR sits near the bottom of the dataset, and it fell further in Q3.***


## Conversion Rate Benchmark — 2026 Year to Date


The median Autos & Vehicles CVR from January through September 2026 was 1.26%, ninth among the 10 published industries.


n=803 active Shopify stores, January–September 2026. Stores with CVR below 0.1% or above 25% excluded. Autos & Vehicles cohort: n=29. Small cohort sizes increase the influence of individual stores on the median. Source: Shogun 2026 Year-to-Date CVR Benchmark Report.


The low CVR is a feature of the category, not necessarily a performance problem. When a shopper is evaluating a car part, an aftermarket upgrade, or a piece of specialized equipment, the session-to-purchase cycle is longer and more deliberate. Comparison shopping, research, and consultation are common steps before checkout. A 1.26% conversion rate in this context likely reflects a real purchase intent rate more accurately than a 3%+ rate would in a consumables category.


The P75 for Autos & Vehicles CVR is 2.13% — the second-lowest top-quartile ceiling of the 10 published industries, after Consumer Electronics (2.01%). The upper end of the distribution is compressed. Even the best-converting stores in this category stay well below the medians of health or food categories. The ceiling is low because the category is low.


> If you’re benchmarking your Autos & Vehicles CVR against the cross-industry median (1.74%), you’re using the wrong number. The category median of 1.26% is the right reference point. A store at 2.13% or above is in the top quartile of its category.


## AOV Benchmark — 2026 Year to Date


The median Autos & Vehicles AOV from January through September 2026 was $601 — the highest of any published category.


n=2,819 active Shopify stores with at least 375 orders, January–September 2026; AOV above $5,000 excluded. Source: Shogun 2026 Year-to-Date AOV Benchmark Report.


The $601 median is nearly double the cross-industry median ($313) and more than $120 above the next highest category, Consumer Electronics ($479). That gap reflects the nature of automotive products: even accessories and parts carry higher price points than most retail categories, and larger purchases — tires, equipment, specialty components — pull the median up further.


January–September 2026, n=100 stores with at least 375 orders; AOV above $5,000 excluded. Source: Shogun 2026 Year-to-Date AOV Benchmark Report, Autos & Vehicles.


## **CVR & Bounce Rate Trend — January 2025 through September 2026**


The graph below shows monthly median CVR and bounce rate for active Autos & Vehicles stores in Shogun’s conversion tracking network.


n=21–27 active stores per month. Each month measured on its own; CVR filter 0.1%–25% per site per month. Small monthly sample sizes mean individual months can move on relatively thin data — directional trends are more reliable than specific monthly figures. Source: Shogun session and conversion tracking, Autos & Vehicles.


The 21-month CVR trend shows a category with real volatility. H1 2025 ran in the 1.47%–1.95% range. Then November and December 2025 came in at 2.03% and 1.91% — November the highest reading in the window. What drove that late-year strength is not clear from the data alone — one possibility is that promotional activity or end-of-year purchasing behavior concentrated buyer intent, but that’s speculative.


January and February 2026 pulled back sharply to 1.23% and 1.41%. March recovered to 1.80%, then Q2 settled into the 1.23%–1.39% range. Q3 dropped further: July 1.06%, August 0.87% and September 0.84%, each well below the same month of 2025. Small sample sizes (21–27 stores per month) mean individual months can move on relatively thin data, but the direction through 2026 is consistent.


Bounce rates are the clearest trend in the data. Through August 2025, bounce rates ran mostly in the 35%–40% range. They moved higher in late 2025 (40%–46%), and through 2026 have climbed to 43%–51%, with July 2026 reaching 50.7%. Q3 2026 averaged about 49%, roughly 9 points above Q3 2025. Whether that reflects changes in traffic quality, page experience, or the types of shoppers reaching the site is hard to say from the aggregate alone.


> ***Autos & Vehicles bounce rates ran in the 35%–40% range through most of 2025, suggesting visitors were engaged. By Q3 2026, they had climbed to 48%–51% — and CVR fell to the lowest levels in the 21-month window. Sustained bounce rate increases of this magnitude are worth paying attention to.***


## **AOV Trend — June 2025 through September 2026**


The graph below tracks monthly median AOV for Autos & Vehicles stores, with each month measured on its own (80–98 stores per month).


n=80–98 stores per month; each month measured on its own (stores with at least 50 orders that month, AOV $1–$5,000). Source: Shogun AOV benchmark data, Autos & Vehicles.


The AOV trend shows noticeable month-to-month movement. The range across the 16 months spans $521 to $649 — a $128 swing. That variability is consistent with a category where individual large orders can move the median meaningfully when sample sizes are in the 80–98 range.


The broad trajectory is upward. June–October 2025 ran in the $521–$570 range. November ($603) and December ($615) were the strongest months of 2025. January 2026 dipped back to $561, then February recovered to $599. April 2026 reached $649 — the peak for the 16-month window.


May and June 2026 ($557 and $553) pulled back from the April peak, and Q3 ran at $567–$612, with September ($612) the strongest month since April. On a matched same-store basis, AOV slipped 3.5% from Q2 to Q3 after its Q2 surge.


On a matched same-store basis (n=71 stores active in both January–September 2025 and January–September 2026), median AOV grew from $554 to $653 — a +17.9% year-over-year increase.


## **What CVR and AOV Are Saying Together**


Autos & Vehicles is the clearest example in the dataset of the inverse relationship between CVR and AOV. It has the lowest CVR of any category except Sports & Outdoors (1.20%) and the highest AOV by a wide margin. Shoppers in this category take longer to decide and spend more when they do. That’s the shape of a considered purchase.


2026 has pulled the two metrics further apart. In Q2, CVR dipped slightly (−0.8%) while AOV surged (+13.3%). In Q3, CVR fell sharply (−33.6% among matched stores) while AOV gave back only a little (−3.5%), leaving it 17.9% above the prior year. Whether that reflects higher-priced product lines holding demand, a shift in the types of buyers reaching checkout, or something else is unclear — but the directional signal is worth noting.


For Autos & Vehicles merchants, the bounce rate trend may be the most actionable number in the data. Bounce rates in Q3 2026 ran roughly 9 percentage points above Q3 2025 across the category, and conversion fell to its lowest levels in the trend window. A larger share of traffic is leaving before engaging meaningfully. Strong AOV can make that easy to overlook, so it’s worth tracking conversion and bounce rate on their own in your analytics.


> ***In Autos & Vehicles, CVR and AOV pull in opposite directions relative to the rest of the market. The year-over-year AOV gain (+17.9%) is real and significant — but it came alongside a sharp Q3 CVR decline and a notable rise in bounce rates. Volume and basket size are telling different stories.***
